notes.title: Metaphysics after skepticism and reduction
notes.thesis: A serious metaphysics should begin from the claim that reality is knowable enough to be articulated, richer than any one reductive inventory, and structured enough that dependence, modality, time, and social reality can be studied as real features of the world rather than as mere shadows of language or physics.
notes.summary: The archive needs an explicit starting posture because contemporary metaphysics is often pulled in two opposite directions at once. One direction says metaphysics is illegitimate, empty, or merely verbal. The other says metaphysics is legitimate only if it collapses into the most austere physical inventory available. Both pressures flatten the field.

notes.title: Essence, grounding, and typed fundamentality
notes.thesis: The archive should treat essence, grounding, and fundamentality as the core explanatory triad of metaphysics, while refusing the assumption that there must be one single untyped deepest inventory from which every other aspect of reality is read off without residue.
notes.summary: Contemporary metaphysics has increasingly shifted from asking only what exists to asking what grounds what, what is fundamental, and what things are in virtue of themselves. That shift is one of the field’s strongest advances because it replaces mere census-taking with explanatory structure.

notes.title: Categories of being: substance, process, relation, and structure
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should be category-plural: reality is not adequately described as only substances, only processes, only relations, or only structures, but as an articulated world in which several ontological categories are jointly indispensable.
notes.summary: Many grand metaphysical systems become elegant by overcommitting to one category. Substance metaphysics captures persistence and identity but can underplay becoming. Process metaphysics captures change but can underplay stable bearers. Structural views capture relational order but can underplay concrete individuals. Monisms capture unity but can blur plurality.

notes.title: Powers, laws, and causation
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat causation, laws, and powers as a linked explanatory cluster: laws should not be mere brute regularities if stronger grounding is available, and causes should be understood in a way answerable both to worldly production and to the structured capacities of things.
notes.summary: Metaphysics becomes sterile when it treats laws as accidental summaries and causation as merely a projection of human inference. But it also becomes dogmatic when it assumes one tidy model of causation fits every domain. The archive needs a middle path that preserves objective structure without pretending every causal problem is solved.

notes.title: Time, persistence, and historical being
notes.thesis: Metaphysics should treat temporality as load-bearing: reality is not fully intelligible unless it can explain change, persistence, succession, and historical constitution, and no single persistence model should be presumed to fit every kind of being.
notes.summary: Many metaphysical pictures look stable only because time is underdescribed. But the world we inhabit includes birth, decay, development, memory, anticipation, institution-building, and irreversible history. A metaphysics that cannot say how beings persist and transform through time will either evacuate change or trivialize identity.

notes.title: Emergence, levels, and non-eliminative reality
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should treat emergence as the joint presence of dependence and autonomy: higher-level realities are often grounded in lower-level conditions without being thereby explained away, and metaphysical seriousness requires criteria for when that autonomy is real rather than rhetorical.
notes.summary: “Emergence” is often used either as a magic wand or as a term of dismissal. The archive needs neither. It needs a disciplined way to say when wholes, organizations, patterns, or systems have explanatory standing that is not exhausted by a lower-level vocabulary, even though they depend on a lower-level basis.

notes.title: Social and normative reality without fictionalism
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat social and normative realities as genuinely real but non-fundamental: institutions, statuses, obligations, permissions, and collective structures are constituted through practices, recognitional structures, and histories, yet they are not thereby mere fictions.
notes.summary: Metaphysics often becomes implausible when it handles the social world badly. If it says only basic physics is real, then marriages, borders, debts, laws, offices, promises, and norms become at best convenient illusions. If it swings the other way and makes social reality free-floating, it loses the dependence of institutions on material, psychological, historical, and recognitional conditions.

notes.title: Theory portfolio and adjudication matrix
notes.thesis: The archive should organize metaphysics as a disciplined portfolio rather than a single prematurely crowned doctrine, while treating a layered, category-plural, essence-and-grounding-centered realism as the current leading synthesis under active pressure from monist, process, and strongly naturalistic rivals.
notes.summary: Metaphysics becomes fragile when it confuses elegance with victory. The archive needs an explicit portfolio so that alternative systems remain visible, comparable, and pressure-tested instead of being erased by local enthusiasm.

notes.title: Modality, world-structure, and truthmakers
notes.thesis: A salient non-skeptical metaphysics should treat modal structure as real but not automatically as a separate realm of objects: possibility and necessity are features of reality’s articulation, possible-worlds talk is often a modeling device rather than an ontological verdict, and truthmaker discipline helps keep modal claims answerable to being.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on modality whenever it speaks of essence, persistence, laws, powers, and grounding. But without a dedicated modal note, the archive risks using modal vocabulary while leaving unclear what sort of metaphysical work it is meant to do.

notes.title: Composition, constitution, and formed wholes
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should sharply distinguish parthood, composition, constitution, and identity, while treating many ordinary and organized wholes as real formed beings rather than as either mere verbal conveniences or uncontrolled explosions of coincident entities.
notes.summary: The archive already speaks about substances, emergence, and historical beings, but those commitments remain unstable unless it can say when wholes exist, how they are related to their material bases, and why some organized entities are more than arbitrary heaps without becoming spooky additions to the world.

notes.title: Properties, universals, tropes, and individuation
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should treat properties and relations as real features of being, and should prefer a disciplined middle posture on which repeatable qualitative natures and particularized instances both do explanatory work in accounting for similarity, causation, and individuation.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on essences, powers, laws, structures, and formed wholes. But those commitments remain underdescribed unless the archive can say what kinds of features things have, how qualitative recurrence is possible, why this redness and that redness are alike, and what helps make one bearer this individual rather than another.

notes.title: Identity, discernibility, sortals, and thisness
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should treat numerical identity as strict but not self-interpreting, pairing it with sortal and historical criteria of individuation, discernibility discipline, and only cautious appeal to primitive thisness.
notes.summary: The archive already talks about persistence, constitution, modality, properties, and individuation. But those debates all quietly presuppose an answer to a deeper question: what makes something the very thing it is, and what counts as a real difference between one being and another?

notes.title: Dependence maps, building relations, and explanatory discipline
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should not speak of “dependence” as if it were one flat relation: grounding, ontological dependence, supervenience, realization, constitution, composition, and causation do different explanatory jobs, and the archive needs an explicit map of those jobs.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on dependence language almost everywhere. Grounding appears in the core explanatory triad, emergence is described through dependence-plus-autonomy, constitution and identity are kept apart, and social reality is treated as grounded rather than fictional. But without a dedicated dependence map, those relations can blur together and the theory starts sounding more unified than it really is.

notes.title: Existence, quantification, and ontological commitment
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should distinguish **what exists**, **what a theory is committed to**, and **what is fundamental**: existence is broader than fundamentality, ontological commitment is a useful but fallible diagnostic, and quantificational form should not be treated as the sole sovereign guide to reality.
notes.summary: The archive already argues that derivative being is real being, that grounding and fundamentality matter, and that social, modal, and higher-level realities can be genuine without being basic. But that posture remains partly underdescribed until the archive says more clearly how existence itself is to be understood.

notes.title: Facts, states of affairs, and structured truthmaking
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should treat reality as **structured**, not as a mere list of objects: propositions are best treated as truth-bearers, facts or obtaining states of affairs as worldly truthmakers, and the archive should distinguish these roles without inflating every truth into a special entity by default.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on truthmaker pressure, essence, grounding, properties, relations, modality, and ontological commitment. But it still lacks one explicit place to say what kind of **worldly structure** is supposed to underwrite truths such as *the statue is fragile*, *the river changed course*, or *the institution now exists*. Without that, the archive risks oscillating between two bad pictures.

notes.title: Abstract objects, mathematical structure, and non-spatiotemporal being
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should treat **abstracta and non-spatiotemporal being** with disciplined seriousness: neither eliminative panic nor cost-free platonist inflation is adequate; the better stance is selective realism in which propositions, mathematical structures, and some other abstract candidates earn their place by explanatory role, structural discipline, and ontological fit.
notes.summary: The archive now speaks confidently about propositions, modality, truthmakers, properties, identity, and ontological commitment. But it still lacks one explicit place to say what to do about **abstract objects** and other non-spatiotemporal candidates. Numbers, sets, propositions, possible worlds, and certain structures keep appearing at the edges of the archive's claims. Without a dedicated note, the archive risks two opposite mistakes.

notes.title: Events, processes, and occurrent ontology
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should adopt **disciplined occurrent realism**: events and processes are real concrete occurrents, not mere shadows of object-talk; but they must be distinguished from facts and propositions, and individuated with enough discipline to avoid redescription explosion or process imperialism.
notes.summary: The archive already says that substances and processes both matter, that time is load-bearing, and that causation cannot be reduced to a thin pattern summary. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say **what happenings are**. Without that, too much of the archive's talk about change, action, history, and causation depends on an underdescribed category.

notes.title: Space, place, location, and boundaries
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should treat **spatiality as real but not automatically fundamental**: place, location, extension, region, and boundary are load-bearing for concrete being, yet space should be handled through a disciplined middle posture between empty-container substantivalism, flat relationism, and easy spatial eliminativism.
notes.summary: The archive already treats time as load-bearing, gives serious room to processes and events, and refuses to flatten concrete beings into a bare census of particles plus predicates. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say **what spatiality contributes to being**. Without that, too much of the archive's talk about continuants, occurrents, constitution, embodiment, environment, and institution-building remains underdescribed.

notes.title: Kinds, naturalness, and world-jointed classification
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should treat **kinds as real but plural, level-sensitive joints in reality**: some classifications answer more directly to the world’s structure than others, yet genuine kindhood need not be monopolized by one fundamental inventory or restricted to timeless “natural” kinds alone.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on essences, sortals, properties, laws, emergence, social ontology, and composition. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say **when a classification is metaphysically serious** rather than merely convenient. Without that, too much of the archive’s talk about species, substances, artifacts, institutions, mental states, mathematical structures, and social categories remains under-described.

notes.title: Teleology, functions, and real directedness
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat teleology as a disciplined dimension of reality: some beings, structures, and activities are intelligible in terms of what they are for, but teleological explanation must be tied to form, organization, history, or agency rather than floated as a free-standing cosmic slogan.
notes.summary: The archive already treats powers, laws, emergence, kinds, social reality, and occurrents as real. But many of those notes quietly rely on directional or purposive vocabulary they do not yet fully explain. Organisms develop toward mature forms, organs have functions, artifacts are for something, institutions are organized around roles and ends, and action is often unintelligible apart from aims. If the archive cannot say when this “for-the-sake-of” language is metaphysically serious, it leaves one of non-reductive metaphysics’ clearest explanatory resources underdescribed.

notes.title: Consciousness, subjectivity, and first-person being
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat consciousness and subjectivity as real modes of being: experience is not eliminable into third-person description, but neither should irreducibility force us into cost-free panpsychist inflation or a return to ghostly substance dualism.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit positions on identity, truthmaking, abstracta, space, events, kinds, and teleology. But it still lacks a dedicated account of **subjects**: beings for whom there is something it is like to exist, act, remember, suffer, attend, and care. That omission leaves several existing notes underdescribed. Identity over time looks different for subjects than for rocks; teleology looks different for agents than for artifacts; social and normative reality depends heavily on creatures who can recognize, answer, intend, and experience.

notes.title: Agency, action, freedom, and reasons-responsive control
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat agency as a real mode of organized power: actions are not mere bodily happenings, free action is not bare randomness, and agential control is best understood through authorship, reasons-responsiveness, and vulnerable self-governance rather than through either passive mechanism or ungrounded will-magic.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit positions on causation, teleology, occurrents, consciousness, and social reality. But it still lacks a dedicated account of **agents**: beings who do things, answer to reasons, initiate or guide conduct, and can sometimes be held answerable for what they do. Without that surface, the archive risks describing subjects as if they merely undergo events.

notes.title: Life, organisms, and biological individuality
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat life and organismic individuality as real modes of organized being: living beings are not mere heaps, machines, or socially projected conveniences, but historically lineaged, boundary-maintaining, self-organizing unities whose reality is compatible with dependence, symbiosis, and multi-level biological complexity.
notes.summary: The archive already leans on organisms in its notes on teleology, identity, composition, space, consciousness, and agency. But it still lacks a dedicated account of **living being itself**. Without one, the archive keeps invoking development, function, embodiment, and bounded unity while leaving underdescribed what makes a living thing more than a complicated arrangement of matter.

notes.title: Potentiality, actuality, and developmental being
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat potentiality and actuality as real modes of being: capacities, readinesses, and developmental trajectories are not mere absences of actuality nor just possible-world bookkeeping, but structured ways beings can be poised toward activity, fulfillment, or change.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on powers, teleology, time, life, and agency. But those notes keep presupposing something they do not yet state directly: many beings are intelligible not only by what they are actually doing now, but by what they can do, are ready to do, are developing toward, or are prevented from doing. Without an explicit note on **potentiality and actuality**, the archive risks treating becoming as either a disguised sequence of fully actual states or a merely semantic modal convenience.

notes.title: Absence, privation, and negative being
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat absences, privations, and some negative conditions as **real but derivative features of being**: holes, lacks, omissions, vacancies, and failures can be metaphysically and explanatorily serious without forcing a shadow ontology of one negative entity per sentence.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on truths about what is **not** the case. A blocked power is a power whose manifestation is absent; an omission is an action not performed; a vacancy is an institutional role not occupied; a hole is a bounded lack in matter; a privation such as blindness is not just any negation but the absence of a capacity natural to a kind of being. Yet the archive still lacks one dedicated place to say what sort of reality such cases have.

notes.title: Intentionality, representation, and aboutness
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat intentionality as a **real mode of directedness**: some states, acts, symbols, and institutions are about things, possibilities, absences, values, or situations, and this aboutness cannot be reduced either to bare causal covariance, formal syntax, or free social stipulation alone.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit positions on truthmaking, propositions, consciousness, agency, social ontology, teleology, and absence. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what it is for a subject, sign, representation, or collective practice to be **of**, **about**, or **directed at** something. Without that, too much of the archive risks relying on contentful language while leaving its metaphysical standing underdescribed.

notes.title: Form, matter, and organized unity
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat **form and matter** as a real explanatory pair: matter is not self-explanatory mere stuff, form is not a detachable ghost, and concrete beings are often intelligible only as **organized unities** whose material basis and formal organization jointly matter.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on form-language in its notes on essence, composition, teleology, life, potentiality, agency, and consciousness. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what form is doing metaphysically and why matter-form thinking remains useful instead of decorative. Without that, the archive risks talking as if organization, unity, and kindhood are real while never making clear whether these are reducible to arrangements of stuff, added by language, or metaphysically load-bearing in their own right.

notes.title: Nonexistent objects, fictional entities, and merely intentional being
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat **aboutness as able to outrun existence** without therefore admitting one full-strength object for every target of thought, story, planning, or impossibility: fictional entities may be real in a derivative and anchored way, but merely intentional, merely possible, and impossible "objects" should not be imported into ontology by default.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit notes on intentionality, structured truthmaking, existence, modality, absence, abstracta, and social reality. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what happens when discourse and thought are directed toward what is not there: Pegasus, Sherlock Holmes, the golden mountain, tomorrow's bridge, the merely planned device, the impossible object, the contradictory story-world. Without a note here, the archive risks oscillating between two bad extremes.

notes.title: Worldhood, totality, and cosmic unity
notes.thesis: A salient non-reductive metaphysics should treat **the world as a real maximal concrete whole and explanatory horizon** without either collapsing all plurality into one full-strength thing or dismissing world-level structure as mere façon de parler: cosmic unity is a live pressure, but derivative plurality remains real unless stronger argument overturns it.
notes.summary: The archive already relies on whole/part relations, modality, fundamentality, truthmaking, space, time, life, agency, and social reality. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what sort of metaphysical standing belongs to **the world itself**: the concrete totality, the maximal context of coexistence and interaction, the possible candidate for priority, and the horizon within which local beings appear as parts, regions, episodes, structures, or domains.

notes.title: Contingency, chance, and open futural being
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat contingency, objective chance, and futural openness as **real modes of how reality can be settled or unsettled**: not every not-yet is mere ignorance, not every contingent truth is brute unintelligibility, and not every indeterminacy is an enemy of explanation.
notes.summary: The archive already has strong notes on modality, powers, laws, time, agency, potentiality, and worldhood. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say how **contingency**, **chance**, and the **openness of the future** fit together. Without that, the datacube risks sliding among three bad options: treating all reality as already fixed and inevitable; treating openness as merely epistemic ignorance; or treating chance as a name for unintelligible breakdown.

notes.title: Intrinsicness, duplication, and local being
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat **intrinsicness** as a real and useful distinction about what a thing is like in itself, while refusing two common overreaches: that the intrinsic is just the non-relational, and that all reality must be recoverable from a perfectly local intrinsic mosaic.
notes.summary: The archive already has strong notes on properties, identity, dependence, space, worldhood, and chance. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what belongs to a thing **in itself**, what belongs to it only through wider worldly placement, and why that distinction matters without becoming a total metaphysical constitution. Without such a note, the datacube risks sliding among three bad options: treating intrinsicness as too murky to matter; treating every relation as therefore extrinsic and ontologically secondary; or treating local intrinsic structure as the whole of reality.

notes.title: Vagueness, borderlines, and indeterminate being
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat **vagueness and borderline status as real pressure points on ontology without assuming that every borderline case reveals a vague object**: some indeterminacy is semantic or representational, some may be worldly, and the archive should distinguish these instead of forcing either false precision or blur absolutism.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit positions on kinds, composition, constitution, identity, boundaries, absence, nonexistence, worldhood, contingency, and intrinsicness. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what should happen when reality or our grip on it seems **borderline**, **soritical**, or **not fully settled at a sharp cutoff**. Without that, the datacube risks three bad slides: precision panic, where every vague case must be forcibly sharpened; blur absolutism, where every difficult boundary is treated as proof that reality itself is vague all the way down; or eliminative escape, where the price of avoiding indeterminacy is to deny ordinary objects, kinds, or boundaries altogether.

notes.title: Concrete individuals, bearerhood, and bundle pressure
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat many concrete individuals as **real organized bearers or thick particulars** rather than as either mere bundles of properties or featureless bare substrata: property-instantiation needs subjects or unities, but those unities should be understood through structured bearerhood, form, history, and organization rather than through a mysterious propertyless hook.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit positions on categories, properties, identity, composition, constitution, form, life, agency, intrinsicness, vagueness, and worldhood. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say **what a concrete individual is supposed to be**. Without that, too much of the datacube’s talk about substances, organisms, agents, artifacts, ordinary objects, and persisting bearers remains underdescribed. The archive needs a stable answer to the pressure question: when many properties are together, what makes them the properties **of one thing** rather than a mere list, and what exactly is the "one thing" supposed to be?

notes.title: Pluralities, collections, sets, and aggregate being
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should distinguish **pluralities, aggregates, sets, and organized unities**: many things together are not automatically one further thing, abstract sethood is not the same as concrete togetherness, and some collective beings earn reality through organization, practice, structure, or action rather than through sheer numerousness alone.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit positions on composition, constitution, worldhood, kinds, social ontology, bearerhood, vagueness, and nonexistence. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what metaphysical difference there is between **many things**, **one aggregate thing**, **a set**, and **a genuinely organized collective or whole**. Without that, the datacube risks sliding too quickly from plurality to objecthood, from counting together to being one, or from abstract collection-talk to concrete ontology.

notes.title: Persons, selves, and practical-historical unity
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should distinguish **organisms, subjects, agents, persons, and selves** while treating persons as embodied, historically extended, socially addressable centers of first-personal and agential life rather than as mere biological units, momentary experiencers, or detached ghost-egos.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit notes on identity, consciousness, agency, life, intentionality, teleology, bearerhood, and plural being. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what metaphysical difference there is between **a living organism**, **a conscious subject**, **an agent**, **a person**, and **a self**. Without that distinction, the datacube risks oscillating between bad extremes: collapsing personhood into bare biology, inflating it into a mysterious extra substance, or treating it as nothing more than social narrative or legal convenience.

notes.title: Psychophysical unity, embodiment, and mental causation
notes.thesis: A non-reductive metaphysics should treat **mental life as embodied, psychophysically realized, and genuinely causally efficacious** without either reducing mindedness to a residue-free physical description or splitting mind and body into two externally glued substances.
notes.summary: The archive now has explicit notes on consciousness, intentionality, agency, life, form, persons, and causation. But it still lacks one dedicated place to say what sort of relation there is between **mental being** and **physical being**. Without that surface, the datacube risks leaving its most important anti-reductive commitments underdescribed. It can say that experience is real, that agency is real, and that organisms matter, while still never saying whether mental episodes are just physical episodes under another description, distinct but lawfully connected properties, emergent organizational features, or signs of a deeper psychophysical unity.
